messages:
Maya R: Quick question — for the new Quick Filters/save-view flow, do we want saved filters to be personal-by-default, or should teams be able to set a route-level default?
Owen K: I'd prefer personal by default, but make it easy to 'promote' to team or route-default. avoids accidental noise.
Lina C: +1 for personal default. Also: telemetry gotcha — if every user saves their own copy we end up with tons of near-duplicates. That skews saved-view counts and makes rollouts messy.
Sam T: We could store a canonical view object and let saved-views reference it. UI shows your "copy" but backend dedups by signature/hash.
Maya R: That sounds good. UX question: how do we present the choices? A dropdown on the Save button? Secondary modal?
Aria D: Design suggestion: inline Save dropdown with three choices: "Save (only me)", "Save for my team", "Set as route default". Keep it one-click for personal.
Owen K: From API side I'd like a simple enum on the SavedView resource: scope: [personal, team, route]. grant_ids: [] for team. route_id optional.
Sam T: API sketch (for reviews):
```json
{
  "name": "Errors > 500ms - mobile",
  "filters": [{"field":"latency","op":">","value":500},{"field":"platform","op":"=","value":"mobile"}],
  "scope": "team",
  "team_id": "team_42",
  "visibility": "shared",
  "canonical_hash": "sha256:..."
}
```
Lina C: If we add canonical_hash, telemetry can reference canonical_id so we can measure reuse vs copies. Add an event 'saved_view.promoted' when a personal view becomes route-default.
Maya R: Good call. Also permissions: route-default should require route-admin or team-admin. We should block regular users from setting org-wide defaults.
Owen K: Agreed. We'll add an authorization check in the save endpoint. Also consider quota: how many saved views per team/workspace? We should cap to prevent abuse (and DB bloat).
Aria D: For the UX, when a user hits the cap show a suggestive modal: "You've hit the saved filters quota. Consider promoting duplicates to a canonical shared view or cleaning up old filters."
Sam T: Migration note: there are ~2.3k existing pinned/quick views in DB that predate scopes. We need a migration to mark them as personal unless they were explicitly created by a team admin.
Lina C: Rollout plan: behind feature flag 'quickfilters-scope'. Backfill script writes canonical_hash for existing ones. Telemetry: emit saved_view.create with fields {scope, canonical_hash, route_id}. Add a daily job to report 'canonical_reuse_rate'.
Owen K: Implementation blockers: dedupe on-write needs to be eventual — we can compute canonical_hash and try to find existing canonical object, create if not found. Race conditions okay if rare.
Maya R: UX copy: when promoting to route-default we should show the impact: "This will change the default view for all users on route X. They can still save personal overrides."
Aria D: I'll mock the Save dropdown and the promote flow. Will include copy and a small 'who will be affected' tooltip.
Sam T: Also add an admin console list for route-defaults so ops can audit and revert if needed.
Lina C: One more telemetry idea: track "view_applied" vs "view_saved" and include canonical_hash to understand actual consumption.
Console Bot: Feature flag 'quickfilters-scope' created by devops at 2151234600.
Maya R: Great — next steps: Aria to provide mocks, Sam/Owen to draft API contract & migration plan, Lina to outline telemetry events. I'll follow up with a short RFC draft by EOD Friday. :+1:
